title: Kew Emergency Help Points
summary: Emergency medical locations, urgent treatment centres, and hazard guidance for Kew and Kew Bridge.
content: For immediate life-threatening emergencies, always dial 999 or 112 first. 1. Nearest 24-Hour A&E Hospitals: West Middlesex University Hospital, Twickenham Road, Isleworth TW7 6AF (from Kew Bridge station: ~30 min walk west along Brentford High Street and London Road, or bus 237 or 267). Charing Cross Hospital, Fulham Palace Road, Hammersmith, London W6 8RF (from Kew Gardens station: District line east to Hammersmith, or bus 190 via Chiswick). For designated Major Trauma care, regional centres include St George's Hospital, Blackshaw Road, Tooting SW17 0QT and St Mary's Hospital, Praed Street, Paddington W2 1NY. 2. Urgent Treatment Centres: West Middlesex Urgent Treatment Centre, Twickenham Road, Isleworth TW7 6AF (co-located at West Middlesex University Hospital). Teddington Memorial Hospital Urgent Treatment Centre, Hampton Road, Teddington TW11 0JL (from Kew Gardens station: bus R68 south). 3. Area Hazards: The tidal River Thames wraps around Kew on three sides; severe flood risk occurs on Kew Towpath, Kew Green, Ferry Lane, and riverside footpaths during astronomical high tides and tidal surges. 4. Supplies: Local pharmacies and retail food stores along Kew Road, Station Parade, and Sandycombe Road provide bottled water, sanitary goods, and emergency first-aid supplies during outages. Note: addresses and opening hours may have changed — confirm on arrival where possible.
